cues: An irony Moyn enjoys: in nineteen seventy four the Nobel Prize in economics was shared by Gunnar Myrdal, who believed the welfare idea could go worldwide, and Friedrich Hayek, the champion of free markets.
One was forgotten; the other saw his fondest wishes come true.
The human rights movement adapted to the new climate, prizing freedom from harm and a minimal state, and the ceiling was forgotten.
